---
title: "iv-provision"
---

You are reading this on **`iv-provision`**, the IV **control-plane host**. That
is a broader job than the name suggests, and this page exists to say so — the
name describes one use of the host's capability rather than the capability
itself.

## What this host does

Its defining property is **control-plane access to exe.dev**: it reaches the
control plane through an http-proxy integration, so it needs no exe.dev SSH key
of its own. Everything below follows from that.

| Role | What runs |
| ---- | --------- |
| **Fleet control plane** | Create VMs (`create-vm`), list them, create and attach integrations, mint scoped tokens. The `create-repo` counterpart makes GitHub repos with no laptop and no `gh` login. |
| **Scheduled fleet checks** | `entire-push-check.timer` (daily) — asserts no repo on any fleet host holds an Entire checkpoint that exists on no remote. Moved here from the mini on 2026-09-15; see below. |
| **This doc site** | nginx serves a published release of this repo on `:8000` behind the VM's exe.dev auth proxy. Re-render with `provision-docsite <repo>`, never bare `render-site` — the live site is a symlinked release, so a failed render cannot break it. |

### Why the checks live here and not on a workstation

`entire-push-check` ran on the mini and failed **every scheduled run**. Host
discovery needs the exe.dev inventory; off-VM that means
`ssh exe.dev ls --json`, and the mini's exe.dev key is served by the 1Password
agent, which auto-locks after 60 minutes. A headless always-on host is locked at
nearly any scheduled moment, `BatchMode=yes` leaves no fallback, and the
integration URL is unroutable off-VM — so both inventory paths failed and the
check failed closed. It looked intermittent only because every success in its
history was an interactive run.

Here the integration supplies the inventory with no key to unlock, so the
dependency is **eliminated rather than worked around**. The general rule, with
the worked cases, is in dotfiles `agent_docs/service-placement.md`: *a probe runs
where its inputs already are; alerting stays off-box.* The healthchecks.io check
deliberately did not move — a dead-man's switch must not share fate with the host
it watches.

One cost, stated rather than hidden: this host has no exe.dev SSH key, so fleet
hosts that never joined the tailnet are unreachable from it and are reported as
`unreachable — not inspected`.

## What this repo is

The IV provisioning layer for exe.dev VMs: a script (`provision-iv.sh`) plus
vendored skills and doc-site tooling that turn a stock exe.dev VM into an IV dev
box.

| File | Role |
| ---- | ---- |
| `provision-iv.sh` | Provisions the IV layer onto the IV base image; writes `~/iv-provision.lock`. |
| `bin/` | `render-site`, `provision-docsite`, `gen-llms-txt`, `entire-push-check` — installed onto PATH. |
| `skills/` | Vendored, pinned team skills — committed so they are frozen. |
| `provisioning/` | Manifests and exclusion lists the fleet checks read. |

::: {.callout-note}
The **repo** keeps the name `iv-provision` regardless of the host's wider role, so
the two are not fully separable by renaming. A host rename was considered on
2026-09-15 and declined — a VM's tailnet node is not freed by rename,
`tailscale set --hostname` does not rename a registered node, and a 2026-07-30
rename left a VM off the tailnet when 1Password locked mid-operation. The
reasoning is recorded in dotfiles `agent_docs/hosts.md`; this page is the cheaper
fix.
:::
